result.title: Graph neural network approach for inferring neuronal connectivity
result.authorString: Gupta A, Neveu CL, Byrne JH.
result.abstractText:
ABSTRACT

Understanding the connectivity of neuronal networks is essential for understanding brain function. Current anatomical mapping techniques, such as serial section microscopy and viral tracing, are resource-intensive and cannot capture the efficacy of connectivity. A complementary approach is to infer effective connectivity from single-neuron-resolution population activity. We developed a graph neural network (GNN)-based tool, CircuitGNN, that accurately infers neural effective connectivity from population activity. CircuitGNN accurately inferred the connectivity of several small circuits and detected both the strengthening and weakening of connections, such as those that occur during learning. CircuitGNN outperformed other methods when applied to simulated population activity generated by an invertebrate central pattern-generating circuit and a cortical microcircuit. CircuitGNN was evaluated on networks of varying size, recording duration, and proportion of hidden neurons. Although performance improved with longer recordings, CircuitGNN achieved high precision with recordings as short as 4 min, scaled to large circuits of up to ~750 neurons, and remained robust when 20% or 40% of neurons were hidden. These results establish CircuitGNN as an accurate and robust technique for inferring neural connectivity from activity.

result.title: Intelligent Bayesian analysis Based on Knowledge Graph and Graph Neural Network for Subway Fire Risk
result.authorString: Wang C, Jin T, Cai D, Hu B.
result.abstractText: As critical urban public transport infrastructure, metro systems have be confined by narrow spaces and dense crowds, attracting global research attention of fire safety. Existed metro fire risk assessment methods have obvious defects: Knowledge Graphs (KG) rely merely on node-edge topology and ignore entity attribute correlations, leading to poor reasoning; classical Bayesian Networks (BN) built by manually selected nodes carry strong subjective bias. To tackle these limitations, this study proposes an intelligent inference framework integrating KG, Graph Neural Network (GNN), and BN. Firstly, a metro fire KG containing 666 nodes is built from historical fire records. Following metro fire codes, Natural Language Processing (NLP) extracts 215 fire characteristic keywords and 6 risk accident labels, embedding feature and label attributes into the KG topology to form a complete dataset. A three-layer Graph Convolutional Network (GCN) is trained for node classification, combined with confidence weighting and K-means clustering. Based on the trained KG-GNN model, an objective data-driven automatic BN node selection approach is put forward, which can intelligent take out metro fire risk evaluation.

result.title: MVMGNN: Multi-View Masked Graph Neural Network for Alzheimer’s Disease Diagnosis using Structural MRI
result.authorString: Yao N, Wang Z, Sun D, Han C, Li Y, Nan J, Zhu F, Zhao C, Zhou W.
result.abstractText: Alzheimer’s disease (AD) is a prevalent neurodegenerative disorder, and early diagnosis is essential for timely intervention. Structural magnetic resonance imaging (sMRI) provides valuable information for characterizing AD-related brain alterations. However, existing sMRI-based brain graph methods often rely on single graph construction strategies, limiting their ability to capture complementary spatial and morphological relationships among brain regions. Moreover, multi-view approaches may introduce redundant features and noisy connections without effective selection and fusion mechanisms.To address these issues, we propose a Multi-View Masked Graph Neural Network (MVMGNN) for AD diagnosis using sMRI data. Brain regions are represented as graph nodes with radiomics features, and two complementary graph views are constructed based on spatial proximity and feature similarity. A joint node–edge masking mechanism is introduced to adaptively select informative feature dimensions and structural connections. In addition, a patient-level cross-view gated fusion module is developed to integrate multi-view representations. Experimental results on the ADNI dataset demonstrate that MVMGNN achieves competitive performance compared with existing methods across AD-related classification tasks. Interpretability analysis further reveals discriminative brain regions and structural connections associated with AD, providing insights into sMRI-based brain network analysis.

result.title: Predictive Anomaly Detection and Self-Healing in Active Distribution Networks Using a Graph Neural Network Digital Twin
result.authorString: Nawaz A, Javid Z, Holderbaum W.
result.abstractText: Active distribution networks (ADNs) are exposed to two anomaly classes that resist unified detection: physical line outages and cyber false-data-injection (FDI) attacks. The standard defense, weighted- least-squares (WLS) bad-data detection, catches FDI but is structurally blind to topology changes, because a reconfigured network still yields internally consistent measurements. This paper identifies a specific property of a predictive graph neural network (GNN): when trained to forecast the one-step-ahead voltage profile, its prediction residual exposes both classes, and its graph structure is what converts that residual into a line-level fault localization, not a more accurate detector. On the IEEE 33-bus feeder across six baselines, the GNN residual records 0 false positives, localizes the faulted line, and reconnects the islanded subtree in one switching action, whereas a CUSUM change-point detector and a graph-agnostic MLP match its detection F1 (0.99 and 1.00) yet provide no localization. The contribution is therefore a specific discovery,the GNN’s graph structure buys fault localization, not detection accuracy, together with the closed-loop self-healing it enables. A reproducible Python pipeline produces every reported number.
